column3: The Hebrew has graves in the plural; BSB has the grave.
The Hebrew has eye in the singular and describes it lodging by their provocations; BSB has eyes gazing at rebellion.
The Hebrew names striking hands in pledge; BSB calls this being my guarantor.
The Hebrew names their heart in the singular; BSB says minds.
The Hebrew states denouncing friends without the added conditional if in BSB.
The Hebrew has peoples in the plural; BSB says the people.
The Hebrew has eye in the singular and all my limbs; BSB uses eyes and my whole body.
The Hebrew has the innocent and godless person in the singular.
The Hebrew says return and come; BSB says come back and try again.
The Hebrew calls them possessions of my heart; BSB says desires.
The Hebrew states light is near before darkness; BSB describes making it seem near.
The Hebrew says I have spread my bed, using a completed action; BSB frames both clauses conditionally.
The Hebrew joins mother and sister with and; BSB says or.
The Hebrew repeats my hope; BSB says any hope for me in the second clause.
The Hebrew has a plural subject for descending to Sheol’s bars; BSB has it and calls them gates.
